SHORT_DESCRIPTION: STREET LIGHTING CO-FINANCING GIZ (DEUTSCHE GESELLSCHAFT FÜR INTERNATIONALE ZUSAMMENARBEIT)
PROJECT_TITLE: Street Lighting Co-Financing GIZ (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit)
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Five innovative Street Lightning LED Retrofit Projects will be realized with the aim to generate best practices models and build capacities in promoting energy efficiency in the public street lighting sector in South Africa. This project will be implemented by GIZ in the framework of their South African German Energy Program (SAGEN). Street lighting in South Africa is a responsibility of municipalities, making up 28-40% of their total electricity consumption as per mainly outdated mercury-vapor (MV) or high-pressure sodium (HPS) lamps. For the overall 3.62m street lights in South African municipalities, Eskom, the national power utility, has estimated average potential overall savings of around 48.5%. However, the major obstacle for the municipalities in South Africa is the lack of capacities to plan, procure and monitor as well as to finance retrofit project implementation in a majority of the 278 African municipalities.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: UNIDO: INDUSTRIAL ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
PROJECT_TITLE: UNIDO: Industrial Environmental Management System
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This project, financed by the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) and implemented by the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), aims at a shift in industrial energy usage practices in South Africa and possibly in the Southern African Region: It will put in place and implement a national Energy Management Standard based on the up-coming Iinternation Organization for Standardization (ISO) standard 50001. The project will facilitate the use of supportive financial mechanisms for energy efficiency, and it will build up national capacities for awareness raising, energy audits and related accreditation and certification services.  The project will deliver - through provincial training and resource centres in Pretoria, Cape Town and Durban - on-the-job training of specialized consultants, 150 industrial energy managers and 2000 staff within three years. This will result in concrete demonstration projects and will help South Africa to get more competitive, reduce its frequent blackouts, improve its carbon footprint, and in the medium term future - as an emerging market - take over more responsibility regarding climate change mitigation.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: ENERGY EFFICIENT STREET LIGHTENING RETROFIT PILOT PROJECT, SCOPING MISSION
PROJECT_TITLE: Energy Efficient Street Lightening Retrofit Pilot Project, Scoping Mission
LONG_DESCRIPTION: Objective of the proposed project is to increase energy efficiency by improving the lighting infrastructure of municipalities, thereby also improving safety in public spaces and contributing to job creation through the establishment of local value chains. In the frame of the SAGEN Programme, GIZ has embarked on technical know-how transfer to the Department of Energy and municipalities e.g. by introducing  baseline calculation methodologies and by advising on the preparation of state of the art tender documents for municipalities in the public street lighting sector. In order to harness the real potential of this innovative technology, it is proposed to support the South African Government (DoE, National Treasury and selected municipalities in the design, implementation and financing of a large-scale roll-out programme of up to 150 000 LED luminaries covering a population of approx. 2 Mio inhabitants and leading to savings of up to 65 Mio kWh per year

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: FEASIBILITY STUDY - EKURHULENI SMART METERING, THROUGH GOVERNMENT OF SOUTH AFRICA
PROJECT_TITLE: Feasibility Study - Ekurhuleni Smart Metering, through Government of South Africa
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This $695,000 grant to the Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality (EMM) supported a feasibility study to evaluate the technical, financial, environmental, and other critical aspects of implementing advanced metering infrastructure in Ekurhuleni, South Africa. The study included the development of a smart metering implementation roadmap and the design of a smart metering pilot project. The implementation of advanced metering infrastructure in Ekurhuleni will promote increased energy savings for consumers while at the same time improving EMM's operational efficiency, customer service, and electricity supply optimization.

SHORT_DESCRIPTION: FEASIBILITY STUDY - WESTERN CAPE GOVERNMENT SOLAR PV PROJECT, THROUGH GOVERNMENT OF SOUTH AFRICA
PROJECT_TITLE: Feasibility Study - Western Cape Government Solar PV Project, through Government of South Africa
LONG_DESCRIPTION: This $545,000 grant to the Western Cape Province's Department of Public Works is supporting a study to evaluate the technical and financial feasibility of implementing a large-scale rooftop photovoltaic project. The study includes a review of South Africa's solar irradiation, the Western Cape electricity market, and solar photovoltaic technologies. The study also includes the development of a conceptual plant design for the project, including a detailed cost estimate, environmental, social, and legal assessments, and tender document preparation. The project will promote clean energy solutions while reducing electricity bills for the province.
